chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Chick Webb as idol and Kaiser Marshall's visit to Miami
summary: He idolized Chick Webb from radio broadcasts, never saw him, and admired Kaiser Marshall's style.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you got to New York, were there any particular drummers, in other bands, that you looked up to? Who were some of them?
Chick Webb was my idol. I never seen the man, but I used to hear the broadcasts from the Savoy when I was in Miami. And I also saw the great Kaiser Marshall,

when he came to Miami with his band -- he brought a band to Miami, and his band was -- Jimmy Powell, the alto saxophone player; at this time, I think Jimmy was about 17 or 18 years old, and that's when I first met him -- down in Miami, with Kaiser Marshall's band.
And Kaiser Marshall really impressed me because he was a sharp dresser, and this guy really knew how to dress, and he was a real ladies' man.
He really got them, I knew him very well.

Yeah, real dapper. And that was another inspiration for me, you know, when I came to New York. And to think that although I idolized Chick Webb's playing, I never did see him in person. When I came to New York, he had taken sick and he was in the hospital, and I never had the pleasure of seeing him in person. But I heard so many great stories about him from fellows that worked with him like Tab Jordan and Elmer Williams, and they used to tell me different things that he used to do on the drums, and I would try to do the same thing when I would play.
